title: approval profile (v1)
description: Profile schema for a surface that asks for a DECISION rather than a reading. Like inquiry/1 it is self-addressed, and it adds the two things a decision needs that an answer does not: a verdict for the set, and a reason the author owes before asking. A document claiming this profile must validate against BOTH the core surface v2 schema and this schema. Documentation: docs/envelopes/approval.md.

id.description: The name the decision is cited by. A commit's Approved: trailer carries this string, and the verdict lands at <reply_to>/<id>.verdict.json, so the hook resolves the citation to a file rather than to a claim. Lowercase, hyphenated, unique within reply_to; a date prefix is the convention that keeps it so.

kind.description: Which decision is being asked for, and therefore which questions the author owed and which the page renders. Two values because two gates exist; a third belongs here only when a third gate does.

reply_to.description: Where the verdict is posted, as owner/repo[:dir]. Same field and same meaning as inquiry/1's: the answer's address, not a claim about where the items should live. The request is conventionally committed beside the verdict it will receive.

reply_ref.description: Branch in reply_to that the verdict commits to. Omit for the repository's default branch, which is the usual case: a verdict is a fact about a moment, so it does not belong on a branch that may never merge.

rationale.description: Why this set of changes should exist at all, in the author's own words, written before the ask rather than in answer to a challenge. This is the field the gate exists to collect: a request that cannot fill it is one whose author has not established that anything is needed.

occasion.description: What prompted the change, from a closed set so the record is countable. new-capability: something can now be done that could not. snag: a logged friction gets its durable fix. correction: a claim here was measured false. cleanup: neither the capability nor the claims move.

session.description: The authoring session's URL, so a verdict read months later reaches the conversation that produced the request.

branch.description: The branch the proposed items live on. The page diffs each item against its base from here, so a request without it can state a change but cannot show one.

commentary.description: Why THIS item, as distinct from the set's rationale. For kind=documentation, what the edit changes about what the document claims. For kind=task, why the outcome deserves to survive this session.

change.description: For kind=documentation: the item's diff, in the core schema's own change block. status and patch come straight from the compare API, so the page renders the same card pages/review.html renders.

deferred_because.description: Required when kind=task: why this cannot be finished in the session proposing it. A task that could be done now and is filed instead has traded a deliverable for a record of a deliverable, and this field is where that trade has to be defended.

related.description: Core schema's related[]. For kind=documentation, the other documents this edit answers to, so a reader can check the change against what already owns the subject rather than judging it alone.
